- Customer impact: demo-quality (sales-blocker) — they are evaluating SLA and reliability.

On Wed, Dec 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick heads up: during this morning's demo with Eden Analytics (Samir Shah), we observed repeated streaming truncation for longer responses when the conversation exceeded ~900 tokens.

Thanks for the detailed repro and request IDs, Logan — that helped a lot. Initial look from infra shows an unusual pattern: several responses have final chunk sizes < 32 bytes and then an immediate stream-close event. Two suspects: our recent continuous-batching heuristic change (patch r3012) that tries to flush partial responses at session end, or an incorrect early KV cache eviction under heavy multi-tenant load.

Immediate asks from runtime side to triage:
1) Can you share the exact API call headers (x-request-id, x-session-id) for the runs? I see the request ids but missing header captures in the zip. If you can forward request-ids.txt as a plain list appended to this thread, that speeds things up.
2) Any customer-side proxy/load-balancer in play? Eden mentioned an edge gateway but not details.

If we confirm it's the batching heuristic, we can roll back r3012 to a hotpatch tonight and redeploy a canary in us-west1. If it's KV eviction, it's a deeper fix (might need a config change for cache TTL on dedicated pools). I'll queue a short investigation and aim to have a triage report by EOD. Sean — can you own the rollout plan if we opt for a hotpatch?

Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks for the data and the quick turnaround, everyone. Short status and plan: we confirmed the abnormal flush behavior is correlated with r3012 continuous-batching heuristics when sessions have the x-client-proxy header present and responses exceed ~800 tokens. That interacts with the streaming flush threshold and produces premature close events on the chunked transfer.

Immediate plan (hotpatch):
- Tonight (18:30 PST): roll back r3012 to previous batching path in us-west1 (canary)
- 19:15 PST: smoke test against the Eden request ids provided
- 20:00 PST: if clean, rollout to full us-west1 serving pool with a blue/green switch (no model restart)
- Post-rollout: monitor for 2 hours; if any regression we will automatically rollback.

Customer messaging draft (short):
"We observed an unexpected interaction between a recent batching optimization and edge proxies that in rare cases caused streaming responses to end early. We will be rolling a targeted fix tonight and will confirm with you as soon as testing completes. We apologize for the disruption during your demo and are prioritizing this."

Please confirm if Sales wants a slightly softer wording for execs. I've attached hotpatch-notes.md with the rollback steps and the canary checklist. Marissa — can you coordinate the customer update and confirm they will retest at 09:00 PST tomorrow? Logan — I'll send a follow-up note when canary completes.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
